previous_statement: Let e=epsilon_r and t=delta-C_pol*(e*delta+delta^2). From C_pol>=1 and C_pol*(e+delta)<=kappa_pol<=1/64, e,delta<=1/64; the root margin gives t>600e. For any T in calU, T^dagger bold-dot T=J and the C*-lower bound give ||T||=||T^dagger||<=(1-e)^(-1/2)<=2. Moreover, for all Y, ||Y||<=e||T||^2||Y||+(1+e)||T||||T bold-dot Y||, by comparing (T^dagger bold-dot T) bold-dot Y with T^dagger bold-dot(T bold-dot Y). Hence ||T bold-dot Y||>=(1-4e)/(2(1+e))||Y||>=6/13||Y||. Finite dimensionality makes L_T bijective and ||L_T^{-1}||<=13/6<3.
new_statement: Take P>=1 and q in (0,1/2] supplied by lem-stage1-polar-retraction and choose C_pol=P, kappa_pol=min(q,1/64), C_grp=600. Let e=epsilon_r and t=delta-P*(e*delta+delta^2). From P>=1 and P*(e+delta)<=kappa_pol<=1/64, e,delta<=1/64; the root margin 600e<t is exactly the second hypothesis for these choices. For any T in calU, T^dagger bold-dot T=J and the C*-lower bound give ||T||=||T^dagger||<=(1-e)^(-1/2)<=2. Moreover, for all Y, ||Y||<=e||T||^2||Y||+(1+e)||T||||T bold-dot Y||, by comparing (T^dagger bold-dot T) bold-dot Y with T^dagger bold-dot(T bold-dot Y). Hence ||T bold-dot Y||>=(1-4e)/(2(1+e))||Y||>=6/13||Y||. Finite dimensionality makes L_T bijective and ||L_T^{-1}||<=13/6<3.
